title: SynVA: A Modular Toolkit for Vessel Generation and Aneurysm Editing
abstract: Intracranial aneurysms (IAs), characterized by unpredictable growth and risk of rupture, are a major cause of stroke and can lead to life-threatening hemorrhages with high mortality and long-term disability. With aging populations, the incidence and overall burden of cerebrovascular diseases are expected to increase, highlighting the need for scalable approaches to analyze complex medical data and improve population-level understanding of these conditions. While digital twins and deep learning offer promising avenues for improving diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment, their effectiveness is limited by the scarcity of large-scale, high-quality medical data and corresponding labels. We present Synthetic VAsculature (SynVA), a modular toolkit for vascular mesh generation and anatomically consistent aneurysm synthesis. SynVA combines novel flow-matching-based methods for generating healthy vessel meshes with learning-based approaches for anatomy-conditioned aneurysm mesh generation; it computes aneurysms from pre-existing vascular geometries rather than generating them in isolation. In addition, we introduce the SynVA procedural model for vascular and aneurysm synthesis based solely on physiological principles and statistical priors, which enables the generation of large-scale datasets. To this end, we release a dataset of 50,000 fully labeled mesh samples for a variety of downstream vision tasks. Extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations show that SynVA generates realistic vessel geometries and anatomically plausible aneurysms, with only minor trade-offs between expert-perceived realism and similarity to real aneurysms. Moreover, pretraining on SynVA data improves point-cloud segmentation and morphological parameter estimation on real data. Code will be released upon acceptance.

title: AI Agents May Always Fall for Prompt Injections
abstract: Prompt injection is the most critical vulnerability in deployed AI agents. Despite recent progress, we show that the prevailing defense paradigm (data-instruction separation) both fails to detect attacks that operate through contextual manipulation and degrades contextually appropriate behavior. We then recast prompt injection via the lens of Contextual Integrity (CI), a privacy theory that judges information flow compliance with contextual norms. This explains types of attacks that current defenses attempt to patch and predict advanced ones future agents will face. We develop unique benign and attack scenarios that force an agent to violate the norms by (1) misrepresenting the flow, (2) manipulating norms, or (3) mixing multiple flows. This reframing suggests an impossibility argument: an adversary can always construct a context under which a blocked flow appears legitimate, or a defender who tightens norms will block genuinely legitimate flows. Our findings suggest that current research addresses a shrinking fraction of future attack surfaces. Instead, through CI, we offer a principled framework for evaluating context-sensitive failures, and designing CI-aware alignment for frontier autonomous agents.
relevance_reason: 本文研究AI Agent的prompt injection安全漏洞，通过Contextual Integrity（CI）隐私理论对攻击进行分类并提出防御框架。内容完全属于安全/对齐领域，与模型压缩、量化、剪枝、蒸馏等任何压缩技术无关，属于hard_gate范畴（alignment/safety方向）。

title: PEIRA: Learning Predictive Encoders through Inter-View Regressor Alignment
abstract: Non-contrastive self-supervised learning (SSL) is an effective framework for predictive representation learning, but popular (and in practice effective) methods such as SimSiam, BYOL, I-JEPA or DINO, which rely on a form of self-distillation to train a teacher-student network, remain poorly understood as they typically do not minimize a well-defined objective. We analyze the dynamics of a variant of the Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) using a regularized linear regressor to predict the learned representations of two views of the data from one another, and fully characterize its stability: non-collapsed stable equilibria align with leading nonlinear canonical correlation subspaces, while collapsed equilibria may also be stable attractors. Motivated by this result, we introduce PEIRA, a non-contrastive SSL method with an explicit objective defined through the trace of the optimal linear regressor. We show that its only stable equilibria are nontrivial global minimizers and recover the same canonical correlation subspaces, with regularization selecting the effective dimension. Experiments on ImageNet-1K and CIFAR-10 show PEIRA is competitive with VICReg and LeJEPA baselines, and qualitative empirical results support the theory. Project page: https://peira-ssl.github.io. Code: https://github.com/MichaelArbel/peira-loss (loss implementation), https://github.com/Basile-Terv/PEIRA (experiment reproduction).

title: TIDE: Asymmetric Neural Circuits for Stabilized Temporal Inhibitory-Excitatory Dynamics
abstract: Recent Continuous Thought Machine (CTM) architecture decouples internal computation from external inputs via neural dynamics, but relies on unconstrained multi-layer perceptrons for its recurrent computations. We propose to model neural dynamics using asymmetric Excitatory-Inhibitory (E-I) networks, which can be stabilized via principles from network theory, while obeying Dale's principle and can be expressed as energy-based systems optimized through a game-theoretic loss. Building on this perspective, we introduce Temporal Inhibitory-Excitatory Dynamic Engine (TIDE), a neuro-inspired architecture that computes internal representations through neural dynamics stabilized by incorporating the Wilson-Cowan dynamics and lateral inhibition. TIDE balances biological realism by, for instance, using Hierarchical Receptive Fields and enforcing Dale's principle to ensure a realistic $80:20$ E-I balance ratio with an end-to-end trainable architecture. The aim of this paper is to introduce a new architecture that brings neuro-inspired learning and architectural principles to the forefront. We present proofs of convergence, stability, and complexity bounds, along with empirical ablation studies. Overall, TIDE achieves higher $\texttt{top-1}$ accuracy than CTM on the majority of the investigated datasets while requiring a smaller training budget. Furthermore, across varying training budgets, TIDE improves $\texttt{top-1}$ accuracy on ImageNet-C by an average of $+1.65$% to $+6.42$% under different perturbation severity levels.

title: BioELX: Context-Aware Cross-lingual Biomedical Entity Linking without Task-Specific Supervision
abstract: Cross-lingual biomedical entity linking (BEL) maps mentions in any language to unique identifiers in a biomedical knowledge base, supporting clinical and biomedical NLP applications. We identify two issues affecting current systems. First, the UMLS (Bodenreider,2004) aliases used to train cross-lingual BEL retrievers are heavily skewed toward English, so retrievers generalize poorly to non-English mentions. Second, although context is often necessary for disambiguation, naively injecting context into retrievers trained only to align aliases severely degrades retrieval. We propose BioELX, a retrieve-rerank framework that addresses both issues. For retrieval, we continue training SapBERT_multi (Liu et al., 2021b) using Wikidata-derived cross-lingual alias supervision, forming shared concept neighborhoods across languages. For reranking, we adapt pretrained LLM rerankers to entity linking through mention-anchored prompting, which marks the target mention so that rerankers score candidates with respect to the intended mention rather than other salient tokens in the context. Experiments show that BioELX achieves new state-of-the-art results on four cross-lingual BEL benchmarks, improving Recall@1 by 4.8 to 18.2 percentage points over prior best results, without any task-specific BEL annotations. Our code and resources are available at https://github.com/AI4MedCode/BioELX.

title: Tree-Guided Identify-Then-Exploit: A Unified Framework of Best Arm Identification and Regret Minimization for Dueling Bandits
abstract: We study $N$-armed stochastic dueling bandits under the Condorcet-winner assumption with a positive global gap, where three widely adopted objectives are considered: best-arm identification (BAI), weak regret, and strong regret. We propose Tree-Guided Identify-Then-Exploit (TG-ITE), the first unified framework to tackle all these objectives to our knowledge. Without requiring transitivity assumptions, we propose a shared tree-guided identification approach to find a high-confidence incumbent within $O(N)$ comparisons. We further propose varied exploitation strategies to utilize this warm-start stage to optimize the specific objectives at hand. For a fixed global gap $Δ$, this methodology enables our approach to (1) build the first winner-stays-style algorithm to achieve $O(N)$ weak regret; (2) realize the joint optimization of BAI and weak regret with $O(N)$ guarantees for both, eliminating the sub-optimal $O(\log N)$ factors of the existing approach; (3) attain the same $O(N\log T)$ order as specialized strong-regret approaches; and (4) achieve $O(N)$ sample complexity in BAI, matching a worst-case lower bound up to an additional $\log(1/Δ)$ term. If a lower bound on the minimal winner gap is known, this term can be removed. Our results suggest that a single identification primitive can serve BAI and both regret objectives with linear dependence on $N$.

title: CausalPOI: Spatio-Temporal Graph-Based Causal Modeling for Cold-Start POI Check-in Forecasting
abstract: As urban environments continue to evolve rapidly, accurately modeling the dynamic behaviour of Points of Interest is essential for supporting data-driven urban planning and commercial decision-making. While recent advancements in spatio-temporal graph learning have improved POI forecasting, most methods rely on proximity-based graphs and correlation-driven modeling, which overlook the functional dependencies between POIs and fail to capture the causal effects of urban interventions. In this paper, we introduce a novel research problem -- cold-start POI check-in forecasting, which aims to predict the future check-in pattern of a newly introduced POI, by modeling its temporal evolution and functional interactions with nearby POIs in a structured urban spatial context. To address these challenges, we propose CausalPOI, a spatio-temporal graph-based causal representation learning framework. CausalPOI leverages Spatio-Temporal Functional Interaction Graph to model semantic and spatial relationships between POIs, and constructs structurally aligned treatment and control graphs to simulate factual and counterfactual scenarios. Extensive experiments on real-world SafeGraph datasets demonstrate that CausalPOI significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across the board, validating its effectiveness in spatio-temporal forecasting, semantic interaction modeling, and causal effect estimation, providing a more interpretable and actionable foundation for urban intervention analysis. Source code is available at Github.

title: StableRCA: Mechanism-Level Root Cause Analysis without Global Graph Discovery
abstract: Root-cause analysis (RCA) seeks to identify the true causal variables that are responsible for a system's abnormal behaviors. A central challenge in this task is to distinguish changes where the anomaly occurs from downstream propagated abnormal effects, particularly when the underlying causal structure is unknown. To address this challenge, we propose StableRCA, an RCA framework that helps distinguish root causes from variables affected by fault propagation by examining how each candidate's conditional distribution, given a selected set of other variables, changes between the normal and anomalous regimes, without requiring knowledge of the underlying causal graph. The method first identifies variables with marginal distribution shifts as root-cause candidates, then selects a local conditioning set for each candidate using stable learning, and finally ranks the candidates by the magnitude of their local conditional shifts, using an importance-weighted Relative Risk Variation (RRV) score as a proxy. Our theoretical analysis establishes sufficient conditions under which comparing the conditional distributions of candidate variables across the normal and anomalous regimes, given suitable conditioning sets, identifies the root causes. Experiments on synthetic benchmarks and four real-world application benchmarks demonstrate StableRCA's competitive performance across diverse domains.

title: CARE: A Conformal Safety Layer for Medical Summarization
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for medical summarization but can omit medically important information and introduce unsupported claims. Existing error-detection methods produce heuristic or uncalibrated scores, providing no formal control over missed errors and no principled way to trade off safety against clinician review burden. We introduce Conformal Assessment for Risk Evaluation (CARE), a post-hoc risk-control layer that adds calibrated omission and hallucination annotations without retraining the summarizer. CARE uses scalar conformal risk control (CRC) to bound the probability that a document contains an unflagged hallucinated sentence, and Learn-Then-Test fixed-sequence testing (LTT-FST) to control the expected fraction of true omissions left unsurfaced for review. Omission surfacing depends jointly on sentence importance and summary coverage, a two-dimensional threshold-selection problem; we show that calibrating one gate and then imposing an uncalibrated second gate can invalidate risk control. Across five medical summarization tasks, mean held-out violation over 100 random calibration/test resplits remains at or below the target for both controllers. At $α=0.15$, LTT-FST achieves the lowest review workload on three of five datasets among omission baselines held to the same confidence guarantee. Review workload varies by task and is highest for long, high-compression documents. On 46 clinician-annotated documents, the calibrated hallucination controller flags 88% of clinician-identified hallucinated sentences. In a preliminary study of 75 clinician reviews, assisted review-time omission coverage increased from 50.4% to 79.0% without increasing review time. Overall, CARE provides a principled framework for targeted, risk-controlled review of LLM-generated medical summaries.

title: LEAF: A Learning-Enabled ADMM Framework for Accelerated Convex Optimization
abstract: We propose LEAF, a learning-enabled ADMM framework for accelerated convex optimization. The key idea is to approximate the Moreau envelope of the objective function using an Input Convex Neural Network (ICNN), resulting in a learned model that preserves convexity and smoothness. This leads to the proposed Moreau Envelope Learning ADMM (MEL-ADMM) and its splitting variant sMEL-ADMM. Unlike existing approaches that learn high-dimensional operators directly, LEAF learns a scalar-valued Moreau envelope, significantly reducing model complexity and improving data efficiency. The framework accommodates a broad class of convex problems with smooth and non-smooth objectives. By embedding convexity explicitly through the ICNN architecture, the proposed approach maintains high approximation accuracy while preserving key structural properties of the optimization problem. Both MEL-ADMM and sMEL-ADMM are developed with theoretical guarantees of convergence and feasibility under the learned model. Rigorous analysis shows that the proposed methods achieve convergence rates comparable to classical ADMM while reducing per-iteration computational cost. Numerical experiments demonstrate up to an order-of-magnitude speedup over state-of-the-art solvers while maintaining low optimality gaps

title: Bellman-sufficient Information Complexity
abstract:
We introduce Bellman-sufficient information complexity for minimax analysis of sequential decision problems. A Bellman-sufficient state retains the history needed for the controlled recursion; an index $Y=χ(Ω)$ specifies which information the bounds charge. A log-penalized Bellman program gives the upper bound, and a Bellman--Fano comparison with an algorithm-dependent reference trajectory gives the lower bound. When admissibility, calibration, and growth conditions hold and the bounds match at a common localization scale, they yield an information-risk sandwich. UCB bounds the immediate decision loss through calibration and optimism, while AMS/EBO gives a robust relaxation of the AIR Bellman program.
  Our main application gives a negative answer to a widely studied form of the GP--UCB minimax-optimality question. For every $0<α<1/4$, we construct a fixed bounded continuous kernel with minimax regret $Θ(T^{1-α})$ along an infinite sequence of horizons. At those horizons, two globally calibrated GP--UCB rules incur linear regret under one fixed truth. A policy that applies action-index AMS to a predetermined finite set in each epoch attains the minimax order; EBO gives a dual interpretation. Many low-value directions inflate the global exploration multiplier even though ignoring them is inexpensive. Through the canonical RKHS feature map, the same construction gives a finite-horizon polynomial minimax gap for the specified maximal-information-calibrated LinUCB rule. A numerical experiment illustrates the mechanism.

title: RAS: Measuring LLM Safety Through Refusal Alignment
abstract: Repeated safety evaluation of open-weight large language models requires generating and judging responses for many related checkpoints. We introduce RAS (Refusal Alignment Score), a representation-based, reference-relative indicator of harmful-request refusal computed by the five-stage SafeVec procedure. SafeVec extracts layer-wise refusal directions from an aligned reference model, measures their alignment in related targets, and calibrates a score from 0 to 100 using behavioral attack success rates (ASR) from reference and calibration models. Subsequent target scoring uses input forward passes alone. Across 18 held-out variants from the Llama, Gemma, and Qwen families, RAS correlates with $100(1-\mathrm{ASR})$ (Pearson 0.934, Spearman 0.851) and achieves 83.0% pairwise ordering agreement. Across five prompt configurations for the Llama reference, directions have mean cosine similarity 0.939. With calibration ASR already available, setup-inclusive evaluation of five targets achieves a speedup of 3.2 to 80.5 times over the specified behavioral protocol. These results support refusal alignment as an efficient signal for screening related checkpoints and prioritizing behavioral audits.

title: Cited Web Sources in LLM Answers about Brands: A Multilingual Audit
abstract: Displayed citations make part of generative search observable, but they do not reveal its complete retrieval process. This audit covers three archived datasets containing 167,551 URL-bearing citation entries across 128 brands, 13 languages and 12 home markets. In the principal Nordic-Baltic component, 3,863 of 21,033 registrable domains account for 80% of 131,514 citations. Wikipedia leads in 11 of 12 query languages. A recovered, separate brand-associated website classification retains 131,512 entries: 108,410 (82.4%) fall outside its brand-associated category and 23,102 (17.6%) inside. This classification does not establish legal ownership. In the full 57-brand Polish aggregate, four recruitment hosts receive 637 citations against 297 for Polish Wikipedia. The results show why normalization, classification rules and denominators belong in citation audits. They describe displayed links without estimating causal effects on brand reputation.

title: DriftGuard: Safety-Aware Multi-Monitor Detection and Selective Adaptation for Evolving Toxicity Moderation
abstract: Automated toxicity moderation systems operate in dynamic online environments where harmful behavior evolves through coded language, shifting targets, and strategic adaptation to enforcement. Existing drift detection methods often focus on global distributional change, but such signals may miss safety-relevant shifts that emerge in localized harm subspaces or high-risk model-error regions. This paper introduces DriftGuard, a safety-aware adaptive moderation framework that combines multi-monitor drift detection with selective model updating. The framework tracks global text drift, identity-harm drift, model uncertainty, toxic-risk drift, and false-negative-risk drift. When safety-relevant change is detected, the model is updated using a hard-mix adaptation set that prioritizes likely false negatives, identity-related high-risk examples, false-positive-risk examples, and uncertain boundary cases. Experiments on Civil Comments temporal shift and Jigsaw-to-DynaHate cross-dataset shift show that safety-aware monitors detect risks missed by global drift alone. Hard-mix adaptation improves toxic recall and accuracy over no-update and random-balanced baselines. It raises toxic recall from 0.8453 to 0.8777 on Civil Comments and from 0.7107 to 0.8523 on DynaHate. Bootstrap analysis further shows stable DynaHate safety gains, with toxic recall increasing by 0.1418 and false-negative prevalence decreasing by 0.0781. Overall, DriftGuard links safety-aware drift detection with targeted, lightweight model updating for more robust adaptive toxicity moderation.

title: Population-Level Profiling of DSM-5 Depressive Symptom Language Among Twitter Users With Self-Reported ADHD or ASD: Exploratory Study Using Natural Language Processing and Statistical Analysis
abstract: Depression frequently co-occurs with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but how depressive symptoms are expressed by people with these conditions is underexplored. We examined whether Twitter users self-reporting ADHD or ASD differ in language related to the nine DSM-5 depressive symptoms. We analysed 1,282,437 tweets (2020-2021) from 792 users. Tweets were screened for depressive relevance by a zero-shot classifier combined with a locally run large language model (Qwen3-8B) and classified into the nine symptoms by MentalRoBERTa fine-tuned on the ReDSM5 corpus. The pipeline was tuned on two stratified samples of 500 tweets and internally validated against human-adjudicated labels on 150 of these tweets. User-level profiles (582 users) were compared with L1-penalised logistic regression, nested cross-validation, bootstrap stability analysis, per-symptom effect sizes, and co-occurrence analysis. A baseline pipeline with a natural language inference filter reached a precision of only 0.09-0.13, whereas the final pipeline reached precision 0.48-0.59 and F1 0.55-0.68. Discrimination between groups was modest (nested ROC-AUC 0.60-0.62). Language related to suicidal ideation was more frequent among ASD users and language related to cognitive issues among ADHD users; both differences were small but robust across sensitivity analyses. These exploratory findings describe how depressive symptoms are expressed online, not their clinical prevalence.

title: Quasi-SVD: Learning a Lie-constrained matrix factorisation for real-time imaging
abstract: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) underlies matrix factorisation tasks across many fields, with imaging applications demanding cost-efficient processing. Yet SVD algorithms are inherently sequential, constraining GPU throughput and limiting online deployment in imaging pipelines. This study introduces a fully parallelized matrix factorization framework for GPUs by enforcing matrix orthogonality on left singular vectors via Lie-parametrised algebra and recovering the remaining components through soft constraints. This asymmetric constraint design enables an efficient parallel decomposition with an orthogonal left factor, achieves high reconstruction fidelity and substantially accelerates computation relative to the exact SVD, with high throughput exceeding standard video frame rates. Performance is evaluated on multiple imaging tasks spanning complementary computational regimes: (1) an MNIST denoising benchmark at an intermediate scale with known ground truth, (2) Mueller matrix polarimetry for neurosurgical tissue characterisation, requiring massive batch processing of small matrices, and (3) spatio-temporal background subtraction for ultrasound localisation microscopy, requiring high-dimensional matrix separation. Across regimes and instruments, the proposed framework demonstrates robust domain transfer at various matrix scales and 2.6--67$\times$ speed-ups over the exact GPU SVD, and, unlike randomised SVD, accelerates large batches of small full-rank matrices. By prioritising downstream reconstruction fidelity over exact spectral recovery, the proposed SVD framework enables GPU-friendly matrix factorisation.

title: Pass the Baton: Trajectory-Relayed On-Policy Distillation
abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) grounds token-level supervision in the student's own trajectory, yet suffers from prefix failure: once the student commits to a wrong reasoning direction, all subsequent generation builds on this deviation, producing misdirected continuations that elicit unreliable supervision and waste compute. We identify a teacher-student continuation asymmetry on failed prefixes, where the teacher tends to redirect while the student continues along the original direction, and convert it into a label-free handoff trigger in Relay On-Policy Distillation (Relay-OPD). During training, Relay-OPD constructs relay trajectories by letting the teacher briefly take over at detected trigger points to produce a teacher leg, after which the student resumes and is optimized on the resulting trajectory. A limited relay budget concentrates intervention on critical early positions while limiting departure from the student policy. With a Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 teacher and Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B-Non-Thinking students on eight mathematical reasoning benchmarks, Relay-OPD achieves the best or second-best results on every benchmark, outperforming standard OPD by +5.73% and the strongest baseline FastOPD by +1.49% on average for 1.7B, with consistent gains at 0.6B. Training trajectory length is reduced by over 50%.

title: Characterizing Human-Likeness in AI Generated Poetry: A Zero-shot Classification Study
abstract: With the advancement of AI technologies, Generative AI (GenAI) and human written text have become nearly indistinguishable. Additionally, the global standardization of AI chatbots made academic malpractice more frequent. Furthermore, existing research indicates GenAI poems are the most difficult to distinguish even without any modification thus, GenAI poems are naturally deemed human-like by modern detectors. However, the objectivity of such dissertations needs to be verified against modern detection tools but the subjectivity of poetry and the black-box nature of the modern LLMs (Large Language Models) architectures made verification of such work quite complicated. Hence, the main objective of the research is to deduce the attributes of English poetry that contribute classification and misclassification of both human and AI poems and provide corroborating or contradicting evidence to the poetry distinguishability claim. For such characterizations, we propose a Zero-shot detection pipeline with a dataset consisting of both human and AI poems to verify the distinguishability of human and AI creation and extract the aforementioned crucial attributes for accurate classification. Extraction of such attributes provides benefits in two ways: firstly, it reduces the margin of training needed as only the poems based on misclassifying attributes need to be trained and fine tuned and finally provides a critical insight to the GenAI detection dilemma to strengthen the modern detection pipelines.

title: ODEWorld: A Continuous Predictive Architecture via Physical-Time Flow
abstract: In the physical world we inhabit, space and time are fundamentally continuous. However, existing machine learning paradigms for world modeling are largely confined to discrete-time prediction, thereby exhibiting significant inefficiency in capturing the dynamics of physical world. We introduce Physical-Time Flow (PT-Flow), a novel approach that learns a continuous latent velocity field operating in physical time. Crucially, the underlying dynamics of sequential data are parameterized by an ordinary differential equation (ODE) embedded in a well-structured representation space. Under this paradigm, the prediction of future can be recast as temporal integration via an ODE solver in the compressed latent space. Building upon PT-Flow, we construct ODEWorld, a continuous-time latent world model that is both efficient and versatile. By extracting time-variant features and enforcing ODE properties on both the dynamical representation space and the latent velocity field, ODEWorld effectively addresses the long-standing representation collapse issue in latent world model literature. This also enables high-quality image reconstruction even after long-horizon prediction. Moreover, its continuous nature allows for arbitrary temporal resolution and even backward prediction, which is impossible for most discrete-time models. Lastly, ODEWorld can provide rich planning-oriented information to facilitate downstream policy learning. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that ODEWorld successfully reconciles planning-conducive dynamics abstraction with visual realism, excelling in both video generation and robotic control. Project page: https://dstate.github.io/odeworld_website/.

title: Prompt Privilege in Large Language Models: Measuring and Mitigating Barriers to Equitable AI Access
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in healthcare, education, public services, and everyday decision making. They should provide comparable assistance regardless of users' literacy, communication style, or prompt-engineering expertise. However, research on prompt robustness primarily focuses on adversarial attacks, prompt injection, and prompt optimization, overlooking whether semantically equivalent requests receive different responses simply because they are phrased differently. We call this accessibility challenge "Prompt Privilege": users with greater prompting expertise obtain better model performance despite expressing the same underlying intent. To address this problem, we propose the Prompt Equity Score (PES), a metric for evaluating performance consistency across user populations, and the Prompt Equity Transformer (PET), an LLM-based agent that automatically transforms user requests into semantically equivalent prompts while preserving their intent. PET shifts prompt optimization from users to AI systems, serving as an accessibility layer between users and foundation models. Experiments on MedQA reveal measurable prompt privilege, with statistically significant performance disparities between low-literacy and expert-prompting cohorts. Applying PET reduces these differences, with no pairwise cohort differences reaching statistical significance in our evaluation. These results suggest that accessibility-oriented prompt normalization can improve equitable AI access. By introducing prompt privilege as a new dimension of AI accessibility and PET as a practical solution, this work advances system-centered accessibility and provides a foundation for fairer, more trustworthy, and more inclusive AI systems.

title: REFLEX: Reflexive Equilibrium Fixed-point Learning for Endogenous eXchanges
abstract: In over-the-counter corporate bond markets, dealers compete for client trades by quoting bid and ask prices. Tighter quotes attract more business, but also informed customers more likely to trade ahead of adverse price moves, leaving the dealer holding the risk. As dealers increasingly use machine learning to set quotes, they retrain these models on the trades their own quotes attract, creating a feedback loop in which each model reshapes the market that generates its next training data. The question is therefore not only whether a quoting model performs well, but whether the market it creates stays stable as the model learns from it. Existing performative prediction theory gives a sharp stability condition, yet expresses it through abstract properties of the learning objective a trading desk cannot measure before deployment. We introduce REFLEX, a framework that replaces those unobservable quantities with three measurable features of dealer behavior: how strongly trading volume responds to tighter quotes, how sharply the dealer's objective bends around its optimum, and how quickly informed flow increases as spreads narrow. REFLEX combines these into a single retraining modulus, a pre-deployment stability margin estimated from a desk's own quote and execution history that predicts whether repeated retraining will converge or amplify itself. In simulation, predicted and measured stability agree within 8%, and competing dealers increase instability by 1.74x with two and 3.16x with three, as predicted. Where ordinary retraining becomes unstable at modulus 1.21, a structurally anchored correction converges as blind retraining collapses. Calibrated over 36 years of public market data, stability headroom falls roughly 4.4x for investment grade and 4.3x for high yield from calm to crisis regimes. Ultimately, REFLEX turns an abstract convergence theorem into a market-level safety margin.

title: Drift-Aware Multimodal User Representation Learning via Multi-Scale Temporal Modeling and Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
abstract: Understanding user preferences from noisy and temporally evolving social media behaviors is fundamentally challenging due to interest drift, where user preferences shift across time and exhibit both multi-scale temporal patterns and diverse co-existing interests. To address this, we propose DUMoE, a unified framework for drift-aware multimodal user representation learning. Our model consists of (i) a temporal dynamics-aware backbone that captures and integrates static profiles, short-term behavioral signals, and long-term dependencies into a coherent representation, and (ii) a sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) interest adapter that disentangles multiple latent interests via expert specialization and adaptive routing. Each expert models a distinct interest subspace, while a gating network dynamically selects and aggregates a sparse subset of relevant experts for each user. To enable stable and effective optimization, we further introduce a three-stage training strategy that decouples backbone learning, expert specialization, and gating optimization. Extensive experiments on real-world social media datasets show that DUMoE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on both user interest prediction and interaction prediction tasks.Code is available at https://github.com/idvxlab/DUMoE.

title: LLMs Can Design Near-Optimal OR Algorithms
abstract:
We ask whether large language models (LLMs) can design effective algorithms for well-specified operations research (OR) problems. We study inventory control, queueing network control, and assortment optimization, using benchmark instances from recent papers in each area. We evaluate two levels of LLM use: at level 1, the model receives one problem instance and returns a solution for that instance; at level 2, it receives only the problem class description and broad parameter ranges, and returns an algorithm that maps instance parameters to solutions. Human input is minimal: we give one untuned prompt that describes the problem, and the model has access to a Python sandbox tool with a fixed compute budget.
  The strongest model we test, gpt-5.6-sol, matches or outperforms the best method reported in those papers on almost all evaluated instances. This holds even at level 2, where the returned algorithm is fixed before seeing the evaluation instances. Performance also improves sharply across models released less than eight months apart, suggesting that this capability is moving quickly. Thus, for the well-specified operations problems we study, a single untuned LLM query can already produce algorithms competitive with specialized methods. These results suggest that frontier LLMs can be a serious empirical baseline for algorithm design in well-specified OR problems.

title: How Evaluation Choices Shape the Measured Benefit of Online Adaptation in Time-Series Forecasting: Warmup, Learning-Rate Selection, and Adaptation-State Memory
abstract: Online adaptation can help edge time-series forecasting under distribution drift, but its measured benefit is sensitive to evaluation choices. We study six public multivariate streams, including building-sensor and smart-meter data, under a leakage-free streaming protocol. We identify two sources of comparison bias. First, the warmup budget of the static baseline has a two-sided effect on seed-mean curves: insufficient warmup undertrains the baseline, whereas excessive warmup can degrade its pre-drift generalization. Across six dataset-backbone settings, the estimated adaptation benefit changes by 3.0 to 18.8 percentage points (pp) over the 1,000-20,000-step warmup range. Second, comparing SGD with momentum (SGD+m) and Adam at a shared default learning rate conflates optimizer quality with rate sensitivity. We select both the warmup budget and each optimizer's online rate using a held-out pre-drift validation slice without accessing test data. Under this procedure, Adam outperforms SGD+m in 310 of 360 cells, and only 4 of its 360 cells fall below the static baseline. Third, we characterize accuracy against adaptation-state memory and A100-measured per-update latency for full, head-only, and calibration-based adaptation. In the evaluated PatchTST frontier settings, several parameter-efficient variants are nondominated on the adaptation-state-memory axis. These findings support a validation-only commissioning procedure. Code, data, and all reported numbers: https://github.com/keiotakmin/tsf-edge-adaptation

title: The Structure of Quantization Damage in LLMs: Why the Next Bit Should Be Spent Globally
abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) is widely used to reduce the cost of serving large language models (LLMs), but its accuracy cost is uneven and is often tuned per model. We study where quantization damage occurs and how to allocate a small additional precision budget. Using causal mixed-precision intervention as ground truth (raise each layer to 8-bit in turn and measure the accuracy it recovers) across 9 open-weight models in 4 architecture families, we test 3 intuitive hypotheses: that quantization damage lives in task circuits, where the model computes, or in weight statistics. None of them predicts which layers benefit from restored precision. Recovery is instead diffuse: for 8 of 9 models, recovering 75% of the gap takes roughly half the layers; the lone exception, Qwen3-8B, is sharply concentrated. At a matched precision budget, spending it globally on finer quantization granularity beats locally repairing the most recoverable layers for all 8 group-128-compatible models (all but OpenLLaMA, whose width rules out group-128), by 21-52 points, including the concentrated Qwen3-8B. We report 2 secondary findings: the residual is budget-limited (8-bit is near-lossless in our evaluation across RTN, GPTQ, and AWQ), and the location of peak recovery correlates with architecture within a family, though not across families. Within this budget setting, global granularity is a better default than selectively protecting critical layers. More broadly, cheap signals that correlate with quantization damage do not necessarily identify where restoring precision improves accuracy; this must be tested with causal intervention.

title: LLM-Driven Algorithm Design for Quantum Circuit Synthesis based on Binary Decision Diagrams
abstract: Quantum circuits are central to implementing quantum algorithms on quantum devices, where quantum gates must be reversible. Many quantum algorithms rely on Boolean functions, which must therefore be implemented reversibly within quantum circuits. Reversible circuit synthesis provides a way to translate such Boolean functions into reversible circuits. Binary decision diagrams (BDDs) offer a scalable approach to this task, but the resulting BDDs and circuits depend heavily on variable ordering. Existing ordering heuristics commonly minimize BDD size because it is closely tied to the circuit size. However, BDD size is an imperfect proxy for the quantum cost of the synthesized circuit (QCC). We propose \texttt{QuantumEvo}, an evolutionary framework that uses an LLM as a heuristic generator for QCC-aware BDD variable ordering. Instead of predicting orderings directly, \texttt{QuantumEvo} searches over ordering heuristics initialized from multiple heuristic families. Candidate heuristics directly manipulate variable orderings using standard BDD operations and are selected by downstream QCC. The discovered heuristic, HGA-QE, modifies the sifting step inside a genetic algorithm so that the procedure is better aligned with QCC. Across the benchmark set, HGA-QE achieves a 70.9\% tie-or-win rate against the per-function best baseline and is strictly best on 13.5\% of the functions. The results demonstrate broadly competitive QCC performance, with HGA-QE showing a clearer relative advantage in strict wins on the two benchmark suites drawn from sources different from the data used for heuristic discovery.

title: CRFCAN: A Complex-Valued Cross-Domain Residual Network for Joint Channel and Phase Noise Estimation in Sub-THz OFDM Systems
abstract: The coupling between multipath propagation and phase noise (PN) poses challenges for joint channel and PN estimation in sub-terahertz (sub-THz) cyclic-prefix OFDM systems. This paper proposes CRFCAN, a complex-valued residual FFT convolutional attention network for single-input single-output systems using comb-type pilots only. Its shared backbone alternately refines time- and frequency-domain features through complex-valued residual channel attention and PN-inspired multiplicative updates, producing channel and PN estimates in their respective domains. An unfolded PN refinement tail combines least-squares updates with feature-guided complex-valued CNN corrections. Simulation results show that CRFCAN achieves lower channel estimation error and bit error rate than the evaluated baselines in both training TDL-A/B/E + 3GPP RAN4 and TDL-C/D + 3GPP RAN1 generalization settings, together with lower PN estimation error at medium-to-high signal-to-noise ratios. Further tests without fine-tuning demonstrate its applicability across different data modulations, OFDM parameters, channel models, and PN spectra.

title: Shot noise can decide capacity comparisons of quantum models
abstract: Shot noise can decide close comparisons of what quantum models appear able to learn. On an IBM processor, the standard estimate of a capacity measure, the effective dimension, placed a 48-qubit model above about 90% of classical networks with as many parameters at 256 shots per circuit. The split-shot estimate from the same data, which removes the bias of the Fisher matrix and needs no noise model, placed it above 12%. A registered run at six parameter points of a 16-qubit model repeated this: the standard estimate placed the three random points above every classical network, the split-shot estimate above 11 to 22%. In simulation the standard estimate reversed the comparison with the classical median at all 100 random points tried. The inflation is the size that shot noise predicts, and a forecast from a pilot run bounds it from above. For squared loss and a linear readout, the error of the standard parameter-shift estimate of a model's Fisher matrix is an exact polynomial in single-shot statistics. Its leading term grows with the effective rank of the matrix, so the shot budget for a stated precision follows from a pilot run; on hardware the observed errors were 0.85 to 1.09 times the predicted ones. The effective dimension can be bracketed from the data but not pinned down at a practical budget. Capacity reports should state their shot count and use the split-shot estimate.

title: HELENA for 5G NR LEO NTN Channel Estimation: A Comparative Evaluation
abstract: Deep Learning (DL)-based channel estimation has shown high accuracy and low latency in terrestrial 5G NR, but Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs) introduce Doppler and synchronization impairments that may require NTN-specific architectures. We investigate whether HELENA, a dual-attention neural channel estimator originally designed for terrestrial channels, remains effective after NTN retraining and suitable across high-performance and power-constrained inference platforms. Its unchanged architecture is trained on paired receiver-compensated and residual-impaired datasets and evaluated alongside terrestrial-origin, NTN-specific, and classical estimators. HELENA's SNR-averaged Normalized Mean Squared Error (NMSE), computed by arithmetic averaging in linear scale, remains within 0.29 and 0.72 dB of the most accurate learned estimator, AttRNet, in the two conditions, respectively. It outperforms global Linear Minimum Mean Squared Error (LMMSE) under compensation and all evaluated LMMSE variants under residual impairments, although profile-aware filtering achieves lower error under compensation. On an RTX PRO 4500, FP16 TensorRT inference reaches 0.0573 ms 99th-Percentile (P99) latency, below the adopted 0.5 ms estimator budget. On a 10 W Jetson Orin NX, HELENA consumes 66.0% less energy per sample than AttRNet, but its 0.9620 ms P99 exceeds the budget; only the less accurate LSiDNN-48 meets it. Thus, HELENA remains effective without NTN-specific redesign for the evaluated task, while accurate embedded inference remains a latency challenge.

title: Reporting Practice Matters: The Impact of Reference Choice on Chest X-ray Report Evaluation
abstract: Radiologists follow heterogeneous reporting practices. Two radiologists examining the same image and identifying the same clinical findings might nevertheless compose superficially distinct reports, varying in terminology, shorthand, formatting, and level of detail. These variations in reporting norms represent an under-appreciated obstacle in efforts to evaluate AI-based radiology report generation (RRG) models, where machine-generated reports are typically assessed based on their concordance with human-generated references. In this paper, we quantify the sensitivity of established evaluation metrics to variations in reporting practices, revealing impacts large enough to alter the rankings of models. We introduce a radiologist-informed taxonomy of variations in radiology reporting practice and a method (ReRef) that rewrites reference reports along the axes of our taxonomy while preserving clinical interpretation. For instance, when comparing the performance of nine RRG models on MIMIC-CXR using RadCliQ-v1, condensing the discussion of normal findings in the reference reports causes Libra to drop from first to second place while CheXOne rises from third to first. Our results suggest that many current metrics fail to decouple clinical interpretation from conformity to reporting practices and that choosing the "right" references that accurately reflect the desired reporting practices can be important in practice. To support future research, we release MIMIC-CXR-Ext-ReRef, a radiologist-validated dataset of 120 (original, alternative) reference report pairs derived from MIMIC-CXR.

title: Form Over Content In Gradient-Based Data Attribution Methods
abstract: Data attribution methods using gradient similarity are widely used to analyze and select training data for large language models, but what gradient similarity actually measures is debated. Some interpret it as identifying task-relevant skills, while other work reports that surface form is the main factor. We resolve this debate for supervised fine-tuning examples by varying task and answer format independently. Specifically, we render benchmarks in different answer formats, such that datasets can share a task without a format or a format without a task. We find that gradient alignment follows the answer format, as benchmark pairs sharing an answer format align strongly (disattenuated cosine near 0.4), while same benchmarks rendered with different answer format classes show no alignment (near 0.0). We demonstrate that this ordering holds from the earliest pretraining checkpoints through post-training, and across model scales and families. We then analyze the released selections of LESS, a gradient-based data selection method for instruction tuning, and find that each target's selections over-represent the target's own answer format. Hence, we demonstrate that gradient-based attribution methods track format similarity more than task semantics, meaning that such methods, as well as the semantic interpretation of the gradient, should be tested on data where answer format and task vary independently for greater robustness and reliability.
relevance_reason: 本文研究梯度相似度数据归因方法（如LESS）在指令微调数据选择中的行为，发现梯度对齐主要跟随答案格式而非任务语义。这是一个关于训练数据选择方法机制的分析研究，与LLM压缩（量化、剪枝、KV cache压缩等）毫无关联。没有针对任何压缩算法的基准测试或比较，属于纯训练数据分析领域，应直接hard_gate。

title: Attribution Gaps in Zero-Training LLM+OVOD Pipelines: A Fine-Grained Analysis of the CAAP--SNAP Discrepancy
abstract: LAOD and similar zero-training LLM+open-vocabulary-detector (OVOD) pipelines score two things separately: class-agnostic localization accuracy (CAAP) and semantic naming accuracy (SNAP). The two consistently diverge, and nobody has asked why. This paper asks why, on the full 5,000-image COCO-Val split (27,273 detections) rather than the small subset the original work evaluated on. Object visual complexity turns out not to be the driver -- small and occluded objects are, if anything, localized better than large ones. Vocabulary novelty is: once the LLM's wording falls outside the detector's native category set, localization accuracy falls from 80.9% to 31.6%. That drop is not spread evenly across unfamiliar phrasing, though. Almost all of it comes from cases where the novel wording actually names a different object than the one COCO annotated (true synonyms still score 89.3%; semantically unrelated "noise" labels score 12.0%). A closer look at a further failure subset tells a similar story: 78-88% of what looks like complete localization failure is really the model correctly finding a real object that COCO's non-exhaustive 80-category scheme simply never labeled, not hallucination. Swap the detector backbone (YOLO-World for Grounding DINO) or the LLM (Gemma-3 for Qwen2.5-VL) and both the effect and its rough size hold up, so this looks like a general property of the pipeline family rather than a quirk of one model pairing. The upshot is that a large share of the apparent CAAP--SNAP gap traces back to closed-category annotation limits rather than a real grounding failure, which matters for how we detect hallucination, analyze failure modes, and design evaluation for grounded multimodal systems meant to work in the open world.

title: scTrilemma: Balancing Identity, Invariance, and Fidelity in Single-Cell Representation Learning
abstract: Single-cell RNA-seq representation learning is fundamentally label-free: cell identities, states, and contexts are not fixed training targets, so what constitutes signal or nuisance is analysis-dependent. A single representation must therefore preserve biological identity and state, remain robust to nuisance context, and retain the gene-level variation needed for expression analysis, three demands we call the representation trilemma. To tackle this problem, we introduce scTrilemma, a latent-bottleneck VAE that routes expression-derived variation to the embedding, the decoder, or the prior rather than forcing all of it through one embedding. It gates gene tokens by expression, routes the cell representation through the decoder, and conditions the prior on unlabeled pseudo-bulk context, under a single reconstruction objective and without target annotations or auxiliary representation losses. In release-based zero-shot evaluation on successive CZ CELLxGENE Census releases, scTrilemma leads all three demands at once and preserves biological-state, differential-expression, and pathway structure across multiple disease settings. Latent interventions further show that context can be removed at almost no cost to the other demands, leaving identity against fidelity as the remaining tension. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/yunhak0/scTrilemma.

title: Shared Phase and Retention Control for Efficient Adaptive Spectral Recurrence
abstract: Fixed-state spectral recurrences offer constant-memory inference and strong long-range retention through heterogeneous complex modes, but their static transitions cannot selectively filter distractors or adapt to evolving dynamics. Existing input-dependent recurrences introduce selectivity, yet real-valued gates lack adaptive rotation, while fine-grained complex transitions incur substantial projection and data-movement overhead and can expose persistent modes to cumulative drift. To address these limitations, we introduce Shared Phase and Retention Control for Efficient Adaptive Spectral Recurrence (SPARC), which modulates a layer's heterogeneous complex memory through two input-dependent scalars. Each mode retains its learned baseline timescale, frequency, and write response, while a retention-coupled clock damps phase corrections in persistent modes. The same shared signals regulate incoming content through modal gates and retention-dependent normalization. The resulting diagonal affine recurrence supports parallel associative scans for full-sequence backpropagation through time (BPTT) and exact structured Real-Time Recurrent Learning (RTRL), with sensitivity storage and updates linear in the recurrent layer's parameter count. We evaluate SPARC on partially observable continuous control, POPGym memory benchmarks, sequence classification, and language modeling. SPARC places among the top two means across all ten reinforcement-learning tasks. Compared with RG-LRU, it improves permuted-MNIST and sequential-CIFAR-10 accuracy by $10.13$ and $10.66$ percentage points, respectively, reduces held-out language-model perplexity by $2.00\%$, and accelerates mixer forward--backward computation by up to $1.69\times$ at width $D=2048$. Code is available at https://github.com/Botwwt/sparc.

title: Linear Recurrent Memory Suffices to Distil a World-Model Policy for Robot Air Hockey
abstract: Does memory-dependent control need nonlinear recurrent dynamics? We study simulated air-hockey defence under temporary loss of puck tracking. A DreamerV3 teacher outperforms a memoryless policy under tracking loss, and erasing its recurrent state at the moment tracking fails cuts its save rate sharply, so the task requires memory. We distil this teacher into compact recurrent policies with a 64-dimensional state, combining a diagonal linear recurrence with an optional rank-$k$ nonlinear innovation while the observation encoder and action head stay nonlinear. Across five matched seeds, the purely linear recurrent model ($k=0$) matches both the GRU baseline and the teacher throughout the tested range of tracking loss. Increasing nonlinear innovation rank provides no measured benefit. This result comes from a fresh test split that was opened only after all models and analyses were frozen. Under 5\,mm observation noise, without retraining, the linear student keeps a higher save rate than the GRU baseline, while using fewer recurrent parameters and less computation. These results suggest that, for this memory-dependent control task, nonlinear representation learning around a simple linear memory can be sufficient, and that nonlinear recurrent dynamics are not necessarily required.

title: Joint neural inference of dynamics and noise covariance for SDEs driven by weighted sub-fractional Brownian motion
abstract: We develop a computational procedure for jointly estimating drift, diffusion, temporal covariance weight, and covariance exponent from discrete observations of stochastic differential equations driven by weighted sub-fractional Brownian motion. A change of variables in the Euler recursion yields a trajectory likelihood that retains dependence between Gaussian driving increments and includes the Jacobian associated with state-dependent diffusion. The estimator combines neural-network and radial-basis representations with analytic covariance assembly for piecewise-constant temporal weights. Normalizing the temporal weight separates its global scale from that of diffusion. For each candidate exponent, the optimal global diffusion rescaling is obtained in closed form, leaving a one-dimensional profile search. We compare the procedure with two neural likelihood adaptations on identical simulated trajectories across twenty coefficient settings. Under the specified training schedules, it attains the smallest exponent, diffusion, and temporal-weight errors in 19, 16, and 14 settings, respectively. Drift performance is mixed, with the smallest error in ten settings. These results assess the complete estimation procedures under the prescribed observation design and training schedules.

title: Why Does Train-Validation Separation Emerge? Gradient-Allocation Dynamics in Pretrained Fine-Tuning
abstract: During fine-tuning, training accuracy often keeps rising after validation accuracy has levelled off. We explain this growing train-validation gap with a support-transfer account: early updates use structure shared by many examples, whereas later fitting relies increasingly on narrow structure whose benefit transfers less to held-out data, so per-example gradient allocations differentiate as the gap grows. We measure this with two readouts computed from fixed training probes alone, the pooled dispersion $D_{\mathrm{den}}$ of normalized gradient magnitudes and its within-class part $D_{\mathrm{within}}^{\mathrm{wt}}$, and derive sufficient conditions under which allocation dispersion, cross-entropy separation, and the accuracy gap grow together. In a constructed feature hierarchy, raising the sample-private feature share from .3 to .7 raises the final accuracy gap from .185 to .527, and homogenizing per-example gradient magnitudes reduces the gap mainly after substantial fitting (median full-dose changes of -4.91 to -11.79 percentage points when it starts at the three later training stages). In 90 fine-tuning runs of three language backbones on six tasks, both readouts are positively associated with the accuracy gap in every run, and $D_{\mathrm{den}}$ remains positive in 89 of 90 runs after linear detrending; 20 vision runs show the same association.
relevance_reason: 本文研究fine-tuning过程中训练集与验证集准确率分化的原因，提出gradient allocation dispersion作为诊断工具，属于纯机制分析/诊断研究。与LLM压缩（量化、剪枝、蒸馏、KV cache等）无直接关联，没有提出任何压缩算法或配方，不涉及任何标准压缩benchmark（MMLU/GSM8K/HumanEval等）。属于训练动力学分析，完全不符合任何压缩bucket，应hard_gate。

title: Not What a Child Expressed: Auditing the Sign-to-Text Safety Interface in Child-Facing AI
abstract: Automatic sign language translation (SLT) has entered consumer products, turning American Sign Language into English text for dictation, messaging, and queries put to a conversational assistant. Child-facing AI and platform trust-and-safety tooling decide on text, using filters on minor accounts and grooming classifiers that score chat messages. A signing child who uses SLT therefore reaches these safeguards through a translation. We found no publicly documented system in which the two have been jointly evaluated, and the leading deployed SLT model was neither trained nor formally evaluated on signers under 18. Errors that alter negation, participant roles, secrecy, urgency or help-seeking could change a safety decision without disturbing fluency. This paper proposes a Deaf-informed pre-deployment audit of that boundary, with a failure taxonomy, a sanitised scenario schema, four comparison conditions, and four outcome measures. Auslan is the planned first case study.
relevance_reason: 本文研究的是面向儿童的AI中手语翻译（SLT）与安全过滤器之间的接口审计问题，属于AI安全/信任与安全（trust-and-safety）领域，完全与模型压缩无关。没有任何量化、剪枝、蒸馏或KV cache等压缩技术的内容，属于hard gate范畴。

title: A Survey of Flow Matching in Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Flow Matching (FM) has recently emerged as a principled and efficient generative modeling framework for reinforcement learning (RL), enabling expressive, multimodal policy parameterizations via deterministic probability transport. Compared to diffusion-based policies that rely on stochastic denoising chains, FM uses sampling based on ordinary differential equations (ODEs), with learned velocity fields, which can substantially reduce inference latency and simplify the incorporation of RL objectives. As research in flow-based RL rapidly accelerates across offline continuous control, online fine-tuning, and foundation model alignment, the literature has become highly fragmented. In this survey, we provide a comprehensive taxonomy of flow-matching approaches in reinforcement learning. We organize the literature along two axes: the target distribution being modeled (e.g., action policies, value critics, transition dynamics) and the mechanism of RL signal integration (e.g., energy-weighted regression, flow-based policy gradients, and group relative policy optimization). Furthermore, we survey emerging frontiers such as discrete and non-Euclidean action spaces, provide a systematic comparative analysis against Gaussian and diffusion baselines, and outline critical open problems. Ultimately, this survey serves as a foundational roadmap for the next generation of generative reinforcement learning and alignment.
relevance_reason: 本文是Flow Matching在强化学习中应用的综述，核心主题是生成模型策略参数化与RL信号整合，完全不涉及LLM量化、剪枝、KV cache压缩或知识蒸馏等任何压缩方向。属于RL/生成模型领域综述，与本团队关注的模型压缩/推理优化无关，直接hard_gate。

title: Forecasting Brand Mentions in LLM Answers: Frozen Predictions Evaluated from Hours to Weeks
abstract: Companies and agencies now monitor which brands large language models (LLMs) name when buyers ask for recommendations. Answers vary between runs, so a single check can mislead and repeated checks cost money. We extend an earlier 20-day replication to ask how well past brand mentions predict later ones over seven weeks. We froze probabilistic forecasts before each of four prospective collection waves of Gemini 3.1 Pro answers to the same 54 buyer questions: nine question families in English, Estonian and Finnish, each for two markets, with four of 12 tracked brands per question. The waves were collected between 1.5 hours and 52 days after the history used by the earliest forecast, and each scored 648 brand and answer labels from 162 answers. A smoothed per-question history achieved a Brier score of 0.0599 at 1.5 hours, against 0.1131 for a per-brand rate and 0.25 for a constant 0.5. A pooled rate clipped to 0.05--0.95, named as the challenger before its first test, scored 0.0259 after 8 hours, 0.0269 after 30 days and 0.0328 after 52 days. Of the brand and question cells named in all or none of the earlier answers, 94.5% to 97.5% kept that pattern in each later wave, and none switched from always to never or back. With a search instruction, 100 of 162 answers returned search activity, compared with 1 of 540 earlier Pro answers; mentions stayed predictable (Brier 0.0563), and Pro history predicted a smaller model's answers less well (0.0787). Human coding agreed with 298/300 sampled automatic labels; two coders agreed on 99/100 shared items (kappa = 0.98). The results cover one provider family, a fixed candidate set and lexical mentions. They support per-question history as the baseline that any forecasting or monitoring method for LLM brand mentions should beat.

title: Learnable Hodge-Laplacian Driven Mixture of Experts for Steady-PDE Surrogates on Coarse Unstructured Meshes
abstract: Surrogate models approximate the solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) for given geometries and boundary conditions. Conventional Transformer-based approaches typically employ a common feature-mixing mechanism across the solution domain, despite the presence of spatial variations at different scales. In this paper, we propose a mixture of transformer experts that combines a routing mechanism with multiscale supervision. Specifically, the individual experts are routed through a controller that utilizes learnable Laplacian matrices to compute weights, used to define a weighted sum of the experts for the output feature vectors at each point of the domain. Subsequently, a decoder receives the weighted sum of the experts output and predicts the solution fields. During training, the reference fields are decomposed into components at different spatial scales by repeated smoothing with a mesh Laplacian. We evaluate our approach on the official AirFRANS dataset using remeshed solution domains leading to unstructured triangular meshes of $4.9$k vertices. The experimental outcomes reveal lower mean relative $L_2$ error and interior mean squared errors among the compared models of this study. Code and data are publicly available in https://github.com/snousias/hodge-moe-pde
relevance_reason: 本文提出基于可学习Hodge-Laplacian的Mixture of Experts用于PDE代理模型，目标是在非结构化网格上近似偏微分方程的解（AirFRANS流体仿真数据集），与LLM压缩、量化、剪枝、KV cache等任何压缩方向完全无关。虽然涉及MoE架构，但应用领域是科学计算/流体力学代理模型，不是语言模型。属于hard_gate。

title: Cross-Precision Transfer, Non-Local Context, and Capacity-Readout Boundaries of Scale Calibration in Low-Bit LLMs
abstract: Low-bit post-training quantization freezes integer codes and zero points, leaving groupwise scales as a compact adaptation interface. We study cross-precision transfer, non-local context, optimizer capacity, and readout behavior on Qwen3-1.7B and Llama-3.2-3B. First, transferring relative scale gains between floating-point and INT3 Qwen models with zero recipient training retains 76.9%-90.5% of self-calibration NLL reductions on fresh WikiText and C4, alongside resolved own-source preferences. Group permutation destroys transfer, and norm-matched layer withdrawal degrades all 16 layer-domain comparisons. A Llama control with identical initial tensors at all calibrated projections isolates preferences induced by surrounding network context. Second, expanding Llama calibration from 4 to 196 projections (0.79M to 22.02M scales) makes learning rate 0.01 win a 50-step training-loss pilot. Continuing to 200 steps memorizes the 28-block WikiText pool, inflates unseen perplexity by 2.06-2.28 times relative to 4-site calibration, and degrades mixed-action PIQA accuracy; learning rate 0.001 prevents memorization and restores accuracy. Third, across 24 Qwen ARC readout endpoints, advancing from 200 to 600 steps worsens INT3 teacher KL on plain-text readouts yet improves it under chat wrapping. Cross-fitted four-parameter static option bias explains 71.4%-75.4% of quantized Chat-Space score-shift SSE, versus less than 2.3% on floating point. Subtracting this bias raises INT3 chat teacher agreement from 33.3%-33.9% to 56.6%-57.5% and cuts KL from 4.15-4.42 to 1.18-1.24 nats.

title: Announced Breaks Separate Conformal Reliability from Frequency Calibration
abstract: When the process behind a time series changes on an announced date, like Australia's switch to five minute electricity settlement on October 1, 2021, intervals calibrated before it can stop covering at their stated level. Whether a forecaster needs the next interval to cover or a finished period's share of misses on target decides the restart. We recompute the next conformal interval from post-break forecast errors, and for n independent ones from the same continuous law, its expected coverage error is $O(n^{-1/2})$, the optimal order in a fixed class among methods told the date. For a finished period's share of misses to match its target, we restart adaptive conformal inference (ACI), which on bounded errors brings that share within $O(n^{-1})$ of target if its corrections at a lower limit stay bounded in total, for that period only. After a simulated mean jump of 5.0 standard deviations, recomputed 90% intervals lie an expected 3.5 percentage points from target at the 50th forecast, a third closer than the 5.2 of the best of five adaptive methods. Of 9 announced changes in Texas, Australian and PJM power markets and a Federal Reserve decision, only Australia's switch moves the errors enough for a 5% test at 80% power to resolve a gain from restarting ACI, and dates help restarted ACI only after large changes.
relevance_reason: 本文研究时间序列预测中的共形推断（conformal inference）区间校准问题，针对电力市场等场景中的结构性断点处理。与LLM量化、剪枝、KV cache压缩等任何压缩主题完全无关，属于统计预测方法论，应直接hard_gate。

title: Recursive Semantic Divergence for LLM Agent Consistency
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents with tool use can behave inconsistently across independent runs from identical states. They may call different tools, produce contradictory outputs, or follow divergent strategies. This variability compounds over time and undermines deployment reliability. Existing evaluation metrics primarily measure task correctness via completion-based scores and do not capture consistency in agent behavior across executions. Separately, agent behavior is analyzed either at the token level using probability distributions or at the single-response level using semantic clustering, but neither captures how inconsistency propagates across future turns of a trajectory. We introduce Recursive Semantic Divergence (RSD), a trajectory-level consistency metric adapted from bisimulation metrics in reinforcement learning. RSD measures the expected cumulative semantic disagreement between two independent rollouts of the same agent from the same state, using natural language inference to detect logical inconsistency. It is defined recursively over future states and approximated by a neural network trained on independent rollouts. The learned metric estimates future divergence from the current state, providing a consistency score at each turn without requiring the full trajectory to complete. When used as a reward signal for fine-tuning, RSD reduces AUC coefficient of variation (CV) by up to 30.9% on tau2-bench and 50.5% on ToolSandbox. Across Qwen-2.5 and Qwen-3.5 models, RSD reduces AUC CV in seven out of eight model-benchmark settings, while improving the final task progress in all eight settings.

title: In-Model Context Compression with Agentic Soft Tokens for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents play an important role in solving complex and sustained tasks, with ever-growing interaction contexts. However, these accumulated contexts will raise substantial computational cost and obscure key decision-relevant evidence. Existing methods typically train external compressors or context-management agents to rewrite context as shorter hard-token sequences, but such external selection may not align with the LLM's evolving representation and is necessarily lossy. In this paper, we introduce Agentic Soft-Token Compression (ASTC), a training-free compression method using soft tokens within LLM agent for long-horizon tasks. Specifically, ASTC uses the model's native recurrent dynamics to determine the already absorbed information, leveraging the commonly-used hybrid Gated Delta Network (GDN)-attention. It then carries this information forward as agentic soft tokens while retaining exact values as hard tokens. The resulting compact sequence reduces later-layer computation and yields reusable KV caches, extending the savings across the agent's trajectory. Extensive experiments on long-horizon tasks show that ASTC matches or exceeds the uncompressed agent's accuracy with up to 59.84% fewer end-to-end Attention Pairs, while trained compressors require 12.3 to 194.9 times more Attention Pairs per successful task. These findings highlight agentic soft tokens as a model-native way to carry absorbed context forward as the task representation evolves.
relevance_reason: 该论文提出ASTC，一种基于hybrid GDN-attention架构的soft token上下文压缩方法，定位为agent长程任务的KV cache压缩。但存在多个hard gate问题：(1) 方法依赖Gated Delta Network (GDN)-attention混合架构，这不是标准的Transformer/vLLM/SGLang部署模型，属于特殊架构需求；(2) 评估指标主要是'Attention Pairs'减少量和agent任务成功率，没有任何标准LLM下游benchmark（MMLU、GSM8K、HumanEval、HellaSwag等）；(3) 评估场景仅为长程agent任务，属于RAG/agents/tool-use范畴，不符合核心LLM压缩评估标准；(4) 属于runtime per-step的soft token替换决策，依赖特殊混合架构，无法直接部署到标准vLLM/SGLang生产栈。综合判断：既属于agent/tool-use场景，又缺乏标准benchmark验证，应hard gate。

relevance_breakdown.inference_perf: 减少59.84% Attention Pairs，无标准延迟数字

title: GSPIM: A Temporal-Locality-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting Accelerator with Polymorphic PIM and Multi-Frame Rendering Dataflow
abstract: 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) enables high-quality real-time novel-view synthesis for dynamic scenes, supporting free-viewpoint video, mobile XR, and autonomous systems at the edge. Methods using explicit 4D distributions, keyframe interpolation, or anchor binding share two GPU data-movement bottlenecks. Temporal filtering follows model record loading, wasting LPDDR5 bandwidth on inactive data. Frame-isolated execution also overlooks highly overlapping active sets and depth relationships across adjacent frames, reloading shared attributes when working sets exceed on-chip cache capacity. To address these bottlenecks, we present GSPIM, a temporal-locality-aware 4DGS accelerator for PIM-enabled edge devices. Polymorphic PIM adapts a shared near-memory datapath to representation-specific field layouts and selection procedures. It filters and compacts valid data into contiguous inputs before the GPU accesses complete attributes, reducing ineffective transfers. Multi-Frame Rendering Dataflow reuses active attributes and stable depth relationships within a temporal window, reducing repeated work across frames. Hybrid Dataflow Scheduling overlaps near-memory data preparation with GPU rendering to reduce waiting. Evaluation combines a GPU-PIM model calibrated to Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB with a 1z DRAM physical implementation of the added circuits. Across three 4DGS methods and six dynamic scenes, GSPIM achieves a 4.15x geometric-mean speedup and a 4.99x geometric-mean energy-efficiency improvement over a fully optimized frame-by-frame GPU baseline. The maximum scene-level PSNR difference is 0.011 dB, and the added physical footprint is 18.7172 square millimeters across 32 LPDDR5 dies.
relevance_reason: 本文是一篇自定义硬件加速器论文，主要贡献是面向4D Gaussian Splatting的PIM（Processing-In-Memory）加速器设计，包括多态PIM数据通路、多帧渲染数据流和混合调度等硬件架构创新。论文报告了LPDDR5 DRAM物理实现（18.72 mm²面积）和Jetson AGX Orin GPU-PIM联合模型，属于典型的ASIC/自定义硅设计，不涉及任何量化、剪枝、蒸馏或KV cache压缩算法。根据规则，自定义硅/FPGA/ASIC加速器论文若主要贡献是硬件设计而非压缩算法，应hard_gate。
